_meta.indication: Prophylaxis of cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection and disease in adult CMV-seropositive recipients [R+] of an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, multi-center, double-blinded trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to letermovir or placebo, with study drug initiated from day of transplant until 28 days post-transplant and continued through Week 14 (~100 days).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult CMV-seropositive [R+] recipients of an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with clinically significant CMV infection through Week 24 post-transplant (onset of CMV end-organ disease or initiation of anti-CMV preemptive therapy).
pivotal_trials.n: Efficacy population N=495 (letermovir N=325, placebo N=170); 373 subjects received letermovir in the safety population.
pivotal_trials.result: Clinically significant CMV infection through Week 24 occurred in 18% (57/325) of the letermovir arm vs 42% (71/170) of the placebo arm. The overall proportion who failed prophylaxis was 38% (letermovir) vs 61% (placebo), with a stratum-adjusted treatment difference of -23.5% (95% CI -32.5, -14.6; p<0.001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%, ≥2% over placebo): nausea (27% vs 23%), diarrhea (26% vs 24%), vomiting (19% vs 14%), peripheral edema (14% vs 9%), cough (14% vs 10%), headache (14% vs 9%), fatigue (13% vs 11%), abdominal pain (12% vs 9%). A higher cardiac adverse event rate was seen with PREVYMIS (13%) vs placebo (6%).
target_moa: Letermovir is a first-in-class inhibitor of the CMV DNA terminase complex, which is involved in viral DNA cleavage and packaging.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not presented because efficacy was robust and safety/tolerability issues could be readily monitored and managed.

summary.text: PREVYMIS (letermovir), a first-in-class small-molecule CMV DNA terminase complex inhibitor, was granted Fast Track (2011), Orphan Drug (2011), and Breakthrough Therapy (2017) designations, and received Priority review; it was approved on the first cycle for prophylaxis of CMV in adult CMV-seropositive allogeneic HSCT recipients based on the Phase 3 P001 trial.
